$comment: The five prompts the Librarian sends a model, as every implementation of the Librarian must write them: what each is made from, and its text to the last character. Every Librarian runs every case and fails on a difference, in whatever language it is written. WHAT A CASE STATES. `prompt` says which of the five it is. `from` is what it is made from. `text` is the prompt. `maxTokens` is the token limit it is sent with, and `temperature` the temperature. TWO OF THE FIVE ARE ASKED FOR ELEMENTS, `score` and `reference-suggestions`: each is sent as a request for an array whose every element the provider holds to a JSON Schema, and `elements` states that schema for each, by the prompt's name. What is read from the elements is specs/src/librarian/reply-cases.json's. The other three are asked for text. A TEXT IN PIECES. A text, in `from` or as `text`, is a string. Where it is long enough to be hard to count it is a list of pieces instead: each piece is a string or `{ "repeat": s, "times": n }`, which is s written n times, and the text is the pieces one after another. THE TEXT IS EXACT. Lines are parted by a line feed, and a prompt ends with no line feed. A line that is optional and absent leaves nothing behind, with one exception, in `resource-summary`. One prompt can end in a space, `annotation-summary`. A case shows each. A list of names or of entity types is written with a comma and a space between its items. `score` asks how well each candidate answers a reference. Of `from`: `selected` is the text the annotation selects and `hint` is what its author typed to say what is meant; a case states one or both. The passage is the two with a space, an em dash (U+2014) and a space between them, and the search term is the two with one space between them; where there is one of them, it is both. `motivation` is the annotation's, and `source` the name of the resource it is on. `body` is the text of the annotation's body, where it has one: it is a line only for an annotation that comments (`Comment`) or assesses (`Assessment`). `entityTypes` are the annotation's. `connected` are the names of the resources its resource is connected to, in the order the gathered graph has them: the first five are named. `relationship` is the relationship sentence gathered for it. `candidates` are the candidates, each with its id, its name and its entity types; one with no entity types is listed with `none`. Twenty candidates at most are listed. Which candidates are listed, and in what order, where one is a better match than another before the model is asked, is not this table's: every case's candidates are in an order no such rule changes. `relationship` asks for the sentence that says how a passage relates to what is around it. Of `from`: `passage` is the text the annotation selects. `connected` are the names of the resources its resource is connected to: the first ten are named. `citedBy` are the names of the resources that cite its resource, each once: the first five are named. `siblingEntityTypes` are the entity types of the other annotations on its resource, each once: the first ten are named. `entityTypes` are the annotation's own, and all are named. `resource-summary` asks for a summary of a resource. Of `from`: `name` is the resource's name, `content` its text, `entityTypes` its entity types. With no entity types their line is empty and is still there, so two empty lines follow the first line. A content longer than 2,000 is cut to its first 2,000, and three full stops follow it. `reference-suggestions` asks what to look at next for a reference. Of `from`: `title` is its title, `entityType` one entity type, `stub` a short text already written for it. An `entityType` or a `stub` that is the empty string is absent. A stub longer than 500 is cut to its first 500, and nothing follows it. `annotation-summary` asks for a summary of a passage where it stands. Of `from`: `resource` is the name of the resource, and `before`, `selected` and `after` are its text before the passage, the passage, and its text after. The prompt has the last 200 of what is before and the first 200 of what is after. `entityTypes` are the annotation's: with none, the last line ends with the space after its colon. WHAT A CUT COUNTS is not held here: every text near a cut is of characters of the basic plane, where every count is the same. Add a case here before changing an implementation.
